label: Multiplying
subgoals: Multiplying by ten moves the decimal point one place to the right.
The digits keep their order; only the position of the decimal point changes.
Multiplying by a power of ten makes a number larger, so the point must move right.

label: Dividing
subgoals: Dividing by ten moves the decimal point one place to the left.
Division by a power of ten makes a number smaller, so the point moves left.
The exponent of ten counts the places moved.

label: Checking the Direction
subgoals: The number of places moved equals the exponent when multiplying.
Powers of ten are the reason metric conversions are simple: each prefix step is a factor of ten.
